stock.thesis: Ranked first among today's eligible candidates on free cash flow yield, cash conversion, valuation against its own industry — revenue -2.8% over the trailing year, growth accelerating against the previous quarter, earnings fully backed by cash.

stock.counterargument: The honest counterargument is the sample: this process has not been shown to work, and a single ranking position is not evidence about one company.
invalidation: Quarterly revenue growth falling below -5.1%, the rate it was running at the quarter before.
Cash conversion dropping below 1.0×, meaning earnings stop being backed by cash.
A close below the 200-session average, which stood at $11.56 on the decision date.
risks: The most recent filing covers a period ending 2026-10-19, 30 days before the decision date.
One of the four quarters in the trailing year is the fourth quarter, which companies report only as part of the full year; it is derived as the annual figure less the first three quarters.
Point-in-time fundamentals are built from filings accepted up to 2026-11-18.

earnings.basis: the same fiscal quarter's announcement a year earlier (2026-01-29) plus 364 days

stock.rule: Universe: every US-listed common stock on NYSE, Nasdaq or NYSE American — about 4,700 names from Nasdaq Trader's own file. Eligible means: priced at $5 or more, median daily turnover of $20M or more over 60 sessions, at least 253 sessions of history, a 10-Q or 10-K whose period ended within 200 days, close above the 200-session average, volatility inside the day's 85th percentile, debt no more than 6× operating cash flow, no results announced in the last 2 sessions, and no position already open in the stock or a fourth in the same SIC division. Eligible candidates are then ranked on equally weighted z-scores within their sector group, over the signals that are defined for that group. One position per session, held 21 sessions, a twenty-first of capital each, 10 basis points of cost each way. Fundamentals are read as they stood on the decision date, never as they read today. The score is a ranking position among that day's eligible candidates. It is not a probability, a price target, or a forecast of any return.
stock.validation: The held-out window has not been opened. No claim of an edge is made or implied.

sources.fundamentals: SEC Financial Statement Data Sets (twelve quarters), point-in-time by accepted timestamp, topped up from companyfacts for companies that have filed since the newest data set

stories.title: Nuitka: Compile Python Into a Standalone Executable
stories.excerpt: Learn to compile Python into a standalone executable with Nuitka. Compare standalone and onefile builds, test speed, and see when PyInstaller fits better.
stories.lead:
Nuitka is a Python compiler that turns your code into a native executable. Its distribution modes let you package an application to run on a compatible machine without a separate Python installation. A more common way to do this is to use a bundler like PyInstaller, which ships your application together with the Python runtime and its dependencies. Nuitka instead compiles your Python code to C before building the executable.

That distinction matters when you’re deciding how to distribute a Python application. Depending on your workload and build mode, Nuitka can offer performance benefits, but they come with trade-offs, including longer build times and additional compiler requirements.

stories.title: Elon Musk says record $446m spending on US midterms was 'pretty foolish'
stories.excerpt: The multi-billionaire also said he was "not Maga", distancing himself from the political movement linked to Trump.
stories.lead:
Elon Musk said on Wednesday that he felt "pretty foolish" about the record sum he spent on the US midterm elections, following sweeping Republican defeats.

The Tesla and SpaceX chief executive was the election's top individual donor, giving $446m (£339m) to support President Donald Trump's party, particularly in Texas where many of Musk's firms are based.

Musk, who had backed Trump's second White House bid, also said he was "not Maga" - the Make America Great Again movement associated with the president.

stories.title: Anthropic IPO raises record $81.3 billion on strong AI demand
stories.excerpt: The five-year-old artificial intelligence powerhouse priced its initial public offering at $83 a share, shrugging off growing concern about a possible AI bubble and volatility in tech stocks.
stories.lead:
The artificial intelligence company Anthropic said on Wednesday it sold more than 956 million shares at a price of $83 a piece in a record-breaking initial public offering that makes it one of the most valuable companies in the world.

The five-year-old AI powerhouse raised around $79.4 billion through the offering, exceeding the $75 billion IPO haul of Elon Musk's SpaceX earlier this year. Anthropic said in a statement that "certain stockholders" also sold more than 23 million shares as part of the IPO, bringing the total haul to more than $81.3 billion.

Anthropic's shares will start trading publicly on Thursday on the Nasdaq under the ticker symbol ANT.

stories.title: Gilts v kilts: What is happening with Scottish government bonds?
stories.excerpt: MSPs have heard both the pros and cons of the government's plan to launch its first ever bond to the market.
stories.lead:
Economists have noted that Scottish bonds would be a more costly way of borrowing than existing routes provided by the UK government through the National Loans Fund.

It has been estimated, external that interest rates on "kilts" would be 0.3 percentage points above gilts, plus an additional £2m per bond in administrative costs.

The Scottish government has not released costings, citing market sensitivities, but has insisted, external issuing bonds would represent value for money relative to the costs of borrowing through the UK scheme.

Juniors Lukas Peabody (San Diego, Calif.) and Dean Strauser (Calabasas, Calif.) were each named to the second team, while first-year Clay Carrington (Menlo Park, Calif.) rounded out the Harvard contingent as an honorable mention.
